question_text: Find the fourth vertex of the parallelogram whose consecutive vertices are (2,4,−1), (3,6,−1) and (4,5,1).

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the property of a parallelogram you would use, and say which pairs are the diagonals.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Equate the diagonal midpoints
steps.margin_note: First mark, printed in the book's margin. A parallelogram's diagonals BISECT each other, so the midpoint of AC equals the midpoint of BD. Note the vertices are CONSECUTIVE, so the diagonals are AC and BD, not AB and CD.
lines: We take A = (2, 4, −1), B = (3, 6, −1), C = (4, 5, 1) and fourth vertex D = (a, b, c)
mid point of AC = mid point of BD

recall.must_convey: That the diagonals bisect each other, so the midpoint of AC equals the midpoint of BD.
accept: the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other so the midpoints are equal
mid point of A C equals mid point of B D
since the vertices are consecutive the diagonals are A C and B D
diagonals bisect avuthaayi kabatti midpoints equal
set the two diagonal midpoints equal

steps.why: Bisecting diagonals is the defining property of a parallelogram, and it turns a shape condition into three plain equations.
common_mistakes: Pairing AB against CD, which are SIDES rather than diagonals.
Forgetting that the given vertices are consecutive and choosing the wrong diagonal.

steps.label: Draw the parallelogram
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark but worth drawing. The vertices are given CONSECUTIVE, so the diagonals are AC and BD — the two dashed lines. Reading them off a sketch is safer than reading them off the question.

recall.must_convey: That parallelogram ABCD is sketched with both diagonals AC and BD drawn. Naming the drawing is full credit — it cannot be spoken.
accept: draw the parallelogram and both diagonals A C and B D
sketch A B C D in order with the diagonals crossing
show that the diagonals bisect each other
parallelogram geesi rendu diagonals mark cheyyali
draw the parallelogram with its diagonals

steps.why: In a parallelogram named ABCD the vertices go round in order, so AC and BD are the diagonals and AB, BC, CD, DA are the sides. Getting that wrong pairs the wrong points.
common_mistakes: Taking AB and CD as the diagonals — they are opposite SIDES.
Drawing the vertices out of order so ABCD is not a parallelogram at all.

steps.label: Solve for the fourth vertex
steps.margin_note: Second mark, also printed. The halves cancel on both sides, leaving three short equations that are solved one at a time.

recall.must_convey: That solving the three coordinate equations gives D = (3, 3, 1).
accept: cancel the halves and solve each coordinate to get three three one
a is three, b is three and c is one
the fourth vertex is three comma three comma one
moodu equations solve chesthe D vasthundi

steps.why: Both sides carry the same division by 2, so it cancels immediately — the working is three subtractions once that is seen.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to cancel the 2 and dividing one side twice.
Sign slip on the negative z-coordinate.
